label: Fourth original token of sequences starting '2 ? d/f', strongest on 'g' after 'd'
explanation: Very sparse (63 dev steps; 121 sequences in 1M), original phase only, at t=3 (88% of mass) or t=4. Nearly always the sequence starts with digit '2' (81% of mass), the previous token is 'd' (86% of mass) or 'f', and the current input is 'g' (85% of mass). The biggest activations are all '2 x d [g]' at t=3 (e.g. '2 d d g' at max 1.63, '2 c d g', '2 d f g'). A weaker group (roughly 0.05-0.15 of max) fires on '2 f d [any letter]' at t=3. The same pattern shifted to t=4 ('2 q a d g', '2 z s d g') and '1 d d g' also fire weakly, which explains most of the missed recall. It does not fire on '2 f s x' (no d or g), when <DEL> comes right after '2 f d', or at any delimiter or copy step. Magnitude goes up most with in_tok=g after d at t=3 with the leading '2'. Without the leading '2', or with the pattern one step later, it is much weaker. The predicate is a conjunction of three specific n-gram clauses (dev F1 0.62-0.66), so this is best read as a narrow token-trigram detector for '2 ? d g', not a clean concept.
